questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Arc Length of a Three-Dimensional Spatial Curve
questions.problem:
Find the arc length of the curve $r(t)=⟨2-{t}^{2},\,{t}^{2}+4,\,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}⟩$
from  $t=0$ to $t=4.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{2}}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,2t,\,t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-2t)}^{2}+{(2t)}^{2}+{(t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{t}^{2}} \\  & =3t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $t\ge 0$ for $t\in [0,4].$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{4}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}3t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{2}({t}^{2}){|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Arc Length of a Planar Curve
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095240/assets/162c0d0310cbbb533c30af373820751fc6c5a447127958486571224d7f8ac07a.png)

Find the arc length of the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ from $t=0$ to $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & ={e}^{t}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|{e}^{t}|\sqrt{{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{2({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{2}{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{2}{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{2}{e}^{t}\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\sqrt{2}({e}^{\pi /2}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}({e}^{\pi /2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Arc Length of a Three-Dimensional Spatial Curve
questions.problem:
Find the arc length of the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$
from $t=0$ to $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t))⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{1}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{2}t\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}(1-0) \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
